speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly what kind of bizarre and agitated behavior you have observed in your husband? How long has this behavior been going on?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the patient have any history of substance abuse, particularly with stimulants like cocaine or amphetamines? Has he experienced any recent head injuries, seizures, or high fevers?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical or psychiatric history reported. Social history: Previously employed. No history of substance abuse reported. Married.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal lab results effectively rule out medical causes like thyroid dysfunction or substance-induced psychosis, strongly pointing toward a primary psychiatric disorder. Given the 6-week duration of delusions and disorganized behavior, I am leaning toward a diagnosis of Schizophreniform Disorder, but I need to assess for mood symptoms to rule out Brief Psychotic Disorder or Schizoaffective Disorder. Do you recall if he had any significant mood episodes, such as mania or severe depression, occurring concurrently with these psychotic symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: No significant findings. Denies any drug use, recent travel, or physical health issues.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the psychotic symptoms have persisted for 6 weeks without prominent mood episodes, this duration fits the criteria for Schizophreniform Disorder rather than Brief Psychotic Disorder or Schizophrenia. I will now request a brain MRI to rule out any structural causes before finalizing the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Brain MRI

speaker: Doctor
text: With the MRI normal and medical causes ruled out, the 6-week duration of psychotic symptoms without major mood episodes confirms Schizophreniform Disorder. DIAGNOSIS READY: Schizophreniform Disorder
